Generate UUIDs

Source: R/generate.R
id_uuid.Rd

Generates n UUIDs of a version, version 7 by default, from the operating system's entropy source and clock. R's random number generator is never used, so set.seed() does not change the result.

Usage

id_uuid(
  n = 1,
  version = 7,
  namespace = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  node = NULL,
  random = NULL,
  time = NULL
)

Arguments

n

The number of UUIDs.

version

1, 4, 6, 7 or 8.

namespace, name

Reserved for the name-based versions 3 and 5.

node

For versions 1 and 6, six raw bytes to use as the node instead of the session's random one.

random

NULL to draw from the operating system, or exactly the bytes the version needs, for tests and reproducible fixtures (with time): 16 per value for versions 4 and 8; 10 per value for version 7 (2 seed the counter at a new millisecond, 8 fill the 62 random bits); for versions 1 and 6, 2 bytes of clock sequence and, without node, 6 bytes of node.

time

NULL for the current time, or a POSIXct (or a double of milliseconds since 1970) of length 1 or n.

Value

A zuid vector of n UUIDs.

Details

  • Version 7 (the default): 48 bits of milliseconds, a 12-bit counter and 62 random bits. Values from one session strictly increase (RFC 9562 section 6.2, method 1): within a millisecond the counter increments, and when it would overflow the millisecond advances by one.

  • Version 4: 122 random bits.

  • Versions 1 and 6: the time in 100 ns ticks, a 14-bit clock sequence and a 48-bit node. The clock sequence and node are random, drawn once per session, and the node has its multicast bit set so it is never mistaken for a hardware address (RFC 9562 section 6.10). Values from one session strictly increase in time.

  • Version 8: the caller's 122 bits, through random.

A clock that runs back by up to the option zuid.rollback_tolerance (seconds, 10 by default) keeps generation increasing from the last value. Further back, version 7 restarts at the new time and versions 1 and 6 increment the clock sequence. Values that would pass the last instant the time field holds are a zuid_overflow_error.

With both time and random given, a call is a pure function of its arguments: the same arguments give the same UUIDs, and the session's monotonic state is neither used nor changed. Values within the call still increase.

Versions 3 and 5 hash a name and are not generated yet; parsing them works. Version 2 is not generated: RFC 9562 leaves it to DCE Security.

Examples

id_uuid(3)
#> <zuid_uuid[3]>
#> [1] 01a17064-522d-7599-8f9b-0916ed00c1c5 01a17064-522d-759a-b139-2b0047c3eb37
#> [3] 01a17064-522d-759b-9086-a228efb33679
id_uuid(2, version = 4)
#> <zuid_uuid[2]>
#> [1] 4896ee2c-907e-4c7b-988d-2fc6f9783015 a8cee064-cbf0-4a3b-a442-7b43e92754bd
id_uuid(version = 7, time = as.POSIXct("2022-02-22 19:22:22", tz = "UTC"))
#> <zuid_uuid[1]>
#> [1] 017f22e2-79b0-760f-adce-5d1798c10d66
